subject: Urgent: Crestline service regression after v3.2 quant rollout
messages:
From: Sara Lambert <sara.lambert@crestline.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Chen <michael.chen@crestline.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 May 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: High p99 latency and 5xx spike after yesterday's model push

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95/p99 latency and a small but persistent 5xx rate (~1.8%) in our production traffic starting ~02:30 UTC this morning, right after the model upgrade your team mentioned (v3.2 + int8-mixed quant profile). Throughput dropped ~22% on our hot paths. The errors are primarily timeouts and a couple of decode failures.

This is impacting checkout flows for a subset of users (we're seeing retries from our edge services) and the product team wants an ETA — our execs are asking for a remediation plan and whether you can revert to the previous model.

I attached a small snippet of the API response errors and a screenshot of our latency chart. Let us know if you want us to open a support access window for logs.

Sara
Sara Lambert
Head of Engineering
Crestline AI
attachments: metrics_dashboard.png, api_error_snippet.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, sara.lambert@crestline.ai
Date: Mon, 21 May 2028 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: High p99 latency and 5xx spike after yesterday's model push

Forwarding Crestline's alert — they see p99 latency and ~1.8% 5xx after we flipped v3.2 with the new int8-mixed qprofile. Throughput down ~22%. They asked explicitly about reverting. Please triage.

Immediate asks:
- Confirm whether the rollout included any kernel or scheduling changes tied to the qprofile.
- Recommend rollback vs incremental hotfix.
- Estimated customer impact (SLA minutes) and a suggested commercial remediation (Ben).

Sara — we're on it; adding engineering and CS leads.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, sara.lambert@crestline.ai
Date: Mon, 21 May 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: High p99 latency and 5xx spike after yesterday's model push

Thanks for the ping. Quick notes from CS/ops perspective:
- Crestline is on a reserved Dedicated pool with burst to hosted; they pinned to v3.1 previously and we pushed v3.2 with the int8-mixed qprofile as part of the compatibility rollout last evening.
- They are seeing tail latency on our hot prefix routes (checkout/complete) and a series of 504s.
- I confirmed they've already restarted edge workers and cleared local caches.

Suggested immediate steps (short-term):
1) Open an emergency rollback window to v3.1 for the affected pool (if Jonas says rollback is safe).
2) If rollback delayed, implement routing policy to send critical checkout traffic to a warm fallback variant (v3.1-compatible) via smart routing.
3) Offer Crestline a proactive credit for SLA exposure (Ben — please advise amount).

I can coordinate a logs session at 11:00 PST if needed; ask Crestline to provide a list of example request ids.

Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Reliability & Customer Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, sara.lambert@crestline.ai
Date: Mon, 21 May 2028 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: High p99 latency and 5xx spike after yesterday's model push

Investigation update (quick):
- Root cause hypothesis: the int8-mixed qprofile triggers a fallback code path in the serving runtime for certain long-prefix sequences. That path disables a key attention-fusion kernel and falls back to a slower kernel; on high token loads we see queueing and occasional timeouts. This explains both the latency spike and the small 5xx rate.
- Rollback: safe and fastest. The v3.1 binary and qprofile are still staged and can be reactivated for Crestline's pool within ~20 minutes if we allocate the control-plane ops window.
- Hotfix alternative: we can ship a targeted runtime patch to avoid the fallback kernel behavior, but that will take ~6-8 hours (including canary + verification).

Proposed remediation path:
1) Immediate: rollback to v3.1 for Crestline's reserved pool (20–30 min). This reduces risk and restores throughput.
2) Medium: run a focused test corpus from Crestline against a patched runtime in pre-prod; validate latency and correctness.
3) After validation, re-introduce v3.2 with adjusted qprofile parameters (disable mixed fallback or tune thresholds).

I'll own the rollback and the runtime patch plan. Please approve rollback and give me the greenlight to take the pool offline for a controlled switch.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
attachments: sla_impact_estimate.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: High p99 latency and 5xx spike after yesterday's model push

Agree with rollback as primary mitigation. On commercial remediation: Crestline is on an annual committed plan; recommend offering a 7-day credit on committed usage and a technical review SLA (joint postmortem + perf tuning session). If this becomes a repeated regression we should escalate to an executive credit/contract concession. Sara — does 7 days look reasonable from your end?

I'll prepare a short note for our revenue ops folks and draft the credit memo once we confirm rollback.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales Lead
Redwood Inference

Sara — thank you for the rapid report and the example request ids you sent earlier. We will proceed with the rollback to v3.1 for your reserved pool at 15:30 PST (in ~25 minutes). Jonas will perform the rollback; Irene will coordinate the verification window and logs session.

Next steps you can expect:
- 15:30 PST: controlled rollback to v3.1 (estimated 20–30 minutes).
- 15:45–16:15 PST: verification and smoke tests. Please keep your on-call engineers available for any follow-ups.
- Commercial: Ben will follow up on a 7-day credit for the SLA exposure and schedule a postmortem call for Wednesday.

We regret the disruption and will follow up with a full postmortem and timeline for a safe re-roll of v3.2 with adjusted qprofile thresholds.

Best,
Marissa
